long_biography.plain_text:
Jack Link, founder of the meat snack company bearing his name, arrived at his first trade convention carrying four boxes of samples and wearing a black wool suit. He had not booked a booth. After talking his way inside, he handed out beef snacks and continued selling aboard a bus for delegates. By the end of the ride, he had orders for everything in stock.

Building a national market did not require abandoning Minong, the small Wisconsin town where he had established production. Meat snacks packed substantial value into little space, making truck deliveries economical despite the remote location. A supply of skilled workers also helped the business remain there. Link saw the company as a source of lasting careers in the community.
